title: Eriksson’s slick gamble wins the second Misano night race
dek: Joel Eriksson won Race 2 at Misano by 1.817 seconds from 12th on the grid, the only driver to start on slicks, when rain returned and Edoardo Mortara and René Rast completed the podium.

chapters.title: Rain again, with one point between the rivals
text: Race 1 had left the Mercedes-AMG title rivals separated by a single point. Paul di Resta had won from pole, while Gary Paffett, the championship leader, retired after contact with his team-mate Edoardo Mortara. Robin Frijns took second for Audi and Mortara completed the podium. Alex Zanardi finished 13th on his debut as BMW’s guest driver.

Sunday’s running was due to begin as the first had, with qualifying at 20:00 and the race at 22:30. Rain returned on Sunday evening, heavily enough for the race director to ask drivers for feedback on whether conditions were suitable. With Paffett’s Mercedes #2 and di Resta’s #3 only a point apart in the standings, and a wet track once more, the weather looked likely to decide the order again.

chapters.title: Duval takes his first pole in the wet
text: Conditions improved halfway through the session and lap times fell quickly, then worsened again with three minutes left. Loïc Duval, in the Phoenix Audi #28, was the only driver to break 1m46s, setting a 1m45.766s that put him on pole by 0.320s. It was his first pole in the DTM, and Audi’s first of the season. He said that, unlike on Saturday, the team had decided to stay out for the whole session rather than change tyres.

Mortara’s Mercedes #48 was second and Daniel Juncadella’s Mercedes #23 third, 0.730s off the pace, though the Spaniard went off at the end of the session and hit a barrier. Rockenfeller and Rast were fourth and fifth, which with Müller in seventh gave Audi four cars in the top seven, and Marco Wittmann was sixth as the best BMW.

Paffett was eighth, a second off, but still two places ahead of di Resta, who qualified tenth, 1.160s from pole, after he could not get his first set of tyres working. Zanardi was last, 19th, 4.4s from the front, in conditions that did not favour him. Joel Eriksson’s BMW lined up 12th.

chapters.title: A lone slick start and a stalled pole-sitter
text: The rain had stopped shortly before the start but the track was widely judged too wet for slicks, and Eriksson, in the RBM BMW #47, was the only driver to start on them. At first it looked like a mistake: he lost several seconds a lap and fell well down the order.

At the front Duval bogged down off the line. Mortara took the lead, Juncadella moved up to second, and Duval was third. A number of collisions in the first laps led to investigations, and di Resta received a warning for forcing Frijns off the track. Marco Wittmann’s BMW #11 stopped for tyres as early as the first lap, and with the track drying quickly most of the field made their mandatory stops over the following laps and went to slicks.

chapters.title: Heavens open and a safety car resets the race
text: Just as Eriksson’s pace began to match that of the cars on wet tyres, the rain came back. Wittmann was the first back in for wets, and many drivers followed, while four had not yet stopped and stayed on the wet tyres they had started on: Mortara, Rast, Frijns and Zanardi. Juncadella, who had been second early on, spun on slicks near the pit entrance and recovered under his own power.

The slicks runners had to crawl round to stop for a second time, which gave Mortara a wide lead. Then Lucas Auer’s Mercedes #22 crashed and the safety car came out, wiping out that advantage so that Eriksson, who had made his one and only stop for wets, was now only just behind the top four. For safety reasons the restart was in single file rather than the two-by-two used on Saturday. Farfus’s BMW #15 spun into the wall and was out.

chapters.title: Waiting game pays off for Eriksson
text: After the restart Paffett, running 14th, was sent into a spin when Juncadella collided with him, the second time in two races that he had been hit by a Mercedes team-mate. He recovered no higher than 14th, and the weekend yielded him no points.

The four who had stayed out now had to make their stops. Zanardi’s BMW #12 came in at the end of lap 18 and rejoined behind Eriksson, in fifth. Rast’s Audi #33 followed, then Mortara, with Frijns, the Abt Audi #4, the last of them to stop, late in the race. Every one of them re-emerged behind Eriksson, who had inherited the lead without making a second stop. Mortara, on much fresher tyres, was lapping far faster, and Eriksson’s margin of nearly 20 seconds began to fall.

chapters.title: Eriksson holds off Mortara by 1.8 seconds
text: Eriksson, who started 12th, took the lead only late in the race, but it was enough. He crossed the line 1.817 seconds ahead of Mortara, with Rast 6.493 seconds back in third. Mortara, who had led off the line, thus took his second podium of the weekend. Frijns finished fourth, and Zanardi crossed the line fifth in his second DTM race, 12 seconds ahead of di Resta, who had moved past Duval for sixth. As a guest driver Zanardi was ineligible for points.

Duval dropped to seventh from pole, ahead of Jamie Green, Rockenfeller and Müller. Paffett was 14th, Timo Glock 15th and Juncadella finished a lap down in 17th. Farfus and Auer were the only retirements. The win was Eriksson’s first in the DTM, in his rookie season.

chapters.title: A first win, a guest’s fifth and a new leader
text: Eriksson said he was simply speechless. He explained that the team had taken a risk with its strategy and that it had been hard to keep the car on the track when the rain came back, but that it had been their day. BMW’s motorsport director Jens Marquardt said the team had not been rewarded for a brave strategy on Saturday but had a little luck on its side on Sunday, since the rain was not forecast to fall during the race. At 20, Eriksson became the second-youngest winner in DTM history.

Marquardt called Zanardi’s fifth place at 51 incredible. Zanardi himself said that he had been lucky, but that his pace had been good at times, that he had tried not to hold anyone up and that he had enjoyed the weekend. Mortara, who had two podiums at Misano, said he had wanted badly to win in Italy but had been unlucky with the safety car. Audi’s Dieter Gass was pleased that all six of the marque’s cars had finished in the points in such conditions.

For Mercedes the weekend was a mixed one: a win and a third on Saturday, a second on Sunday, but also three cars lost in Race 1 and a Race 2 in which team-mates collided. Paffett, who said the car had been good in both the dry and the wet and that the team had thrown away its own chances, left Italy without a point. Mercedes team principal Ulrich Fritz listed pit-stop problems for Paffett, driving errors and the collision between team-mates as things that should not happen, and called for a careful analysis of how each had come about, while saying the team could still be satisfied with the weekend overall.

Di Resta’s sixth place was enough to give him the championship lead. He had 186 points to Paffett’s 177, nine ahead, with Mortara third on 138 and Wittmann the leading BMW driver in fourth on 112. Fourteen of the 20 races had been run and three race weekends remained. The DTM would return to Germany two weeks later, for the Nürburgring round on 7–9 September.

facts.t: The only slicks on the grid
facts.v: Eriksson was the only driver to start on slick tyres, and his single stop for wets, after the rain returned, was his first and only of the race.
